channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Meta Offers Zuckerberg New Shares to Shield Him From Wealth Tax
item.description: Meta signed an agreement with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in the same jurisdiction as the company’s headquarters after the CEO said he was weighing leaving California if the state passes a wealth tax. Ed Ludlow has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Comcast Planning Significant Jobs Cuts as Part of Reorganization
item.description: Comcast Corp. is planning a significant number of job cuts as part of an overall restructuring of its cable-TV, broadband and wireless businesses, according to people familiar with the company’s thinking.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis

item.title: Tesla, IBM & Meta Report Earnings as AI Takes Center Stage
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are BlackRock Head of the Americas Institutional Business Armando Senra, CME Group CEO & Chairman Terry Duffy, First Independence Bank Chairman & CEO Kenneth Kelly, October Capital CEO & Managing Partner Frank Baker, Bose CEO Lila Snyder, Man Group Managing Director, Solutions Matt Rowe, Wedbush Internet Equity Research Managing Director Ygal Arounian, ARK Investment Director of Investment Analysis Tasha Keeney, First Founder & CEO Libby Leffler, American Century Investments Multi-Asset Strategies CIO Rich Weiss, & Former Tesla Board Member Steve Westly. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New $4.2 Billion Texas Gas Pipe to Supply Fuel for Data Center
item.description: Kinder Morgan Inc. formally committed to building a $4.2 billion pipeline that will haul fuel across West Texas and the Panhandle to help power a data center complex.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: Encouraged by Meta’s Partnerships, Says First Founder
item.description: Libby Leffler, discusses whether Meta’s history of scaling up new initiatives offers reason to doubt Zuckerberg’s ability to succeed. Leffler discusses Meta’s fourth-quarter revenue outlook of $73 billion to $76 billion, compared with an estimate of $73.57 billion, and noted a new non-voting Class C common stock. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Mandeep Singh on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Boosts Bet on AI With Spending Outlook, New Stock Class
item.description: Meta Platforms boosted its capital spending outlook and announced plans for a new class of nonvoting stock, escalating its already-stratospheric bet on artificial intelligence. Capital expenditures will be $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, the social-media giant said during its quarterly earnings report Wednesday, raising the bottom end of the range from $130 billion. The new class of shares, meanwhile, will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Frank Baker on New Firm, October Capital
item.description: Frank Baker, CEO and Managing Partner of October Capital, discusses the launch of the new firm, formed by tech-focused private equity shop Siris. October Capital will focus on services supporting AI infrastructure, physical security, and financial infrastructure. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla Will Combine, Steve Westly Predicts
item.description: Steve Westly, founder and managing partner of The Westly Group and a former Tesla board member, expects SpaceX and Tesla to combine. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla's Future Is Robotaxis, Says Ark's Keeney
item.description: Tasha Keeney, Ark Investment director of investment analysis, says robotaxis are the future for Tesla. She says the company is well positioned over its peers and the Cybercab is cheaper to operate compared to Waymo's next generation vehicle. Elon Musk's company reported third-quarter profits that beat estimates. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Takeaways From Meta's Earnings and AI Spending Plans
item.description: Ygal Arounian, Wedbush Internet equity research managing director, reacts to Meta Platforms' third-quarter earnings and boosted capital spending outlook. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Is Tailwind, IBM CEO Says as Sales Rise
item.description: IBM says sales increased by 5% to $17.1 billion in the third quarter, topping estimates. Sales in the software unit also expanded. The company reported earnings of $2.95 per share. CEO Arvind Krishna says AI is a tailwind. Romaine Bostick discusses with Mandeep Singh and Anurag Rana of Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SAP Cloud Growth Beats Forecast in Sign of Software’s Resilience
item.description: SAP SE reported higher growth for its cloud products than anticipated in a sign that the boom in artificial intelligence hasn’t undermined demand for the German software maker’s offerings.
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou

item.title: IBM Posts 5% Sales Growth, Says Infrastructure Deals Came Back
item.description: International Business Machines Corp. reported sales that topped analysts’ estimates, saying it had recovered most of the infrastructure deals that were delayed earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Meta Touts AI Progress While Escalating Its Bet on the Market
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg told investors that a pricey wager on artificial intelligence is delivering results, setting the stage for the company to bet even more aggressively on the market.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Texas Instruments Gives Sales Forecast That Tops Estimates
item.description: Texas Instruments Inc., the biggest maker of analog and embedded processing chips, gave a strong revenue forecast for the current period, lifted by demand from automotive and industrial customers.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Bose CEO Lila Snyder on Skullcandy Acquisition
item.description: With Bose acquiring Skullcandy today, CEO Lila Snyder sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss what the deal means for both companies, how the audio company is trying to reach the next generation with wired headphones and the role AI will play in future products. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Plans to Issue New Non-Voting Stock for Capital Raising
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. has established a new class of non-voting stock that it could use to fund its heavy spending on artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: Meta Earnings: Live Results for Q3 2026, AI Spending, Mark Zuckerberg Comments
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Meta to Pay Historic $25 Billion in New Mexico Deception Case
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. was ordered to pay the state of New Mexico a $25 billion civil penalty Wednesday, one of the largest verdicts in US legal history in a case spurred by the decade-old Cambridge Analytica scandal.
item.dc:creator: Isaiah Poritz

item.title: Navy Halts New Orders of Aevex Drone Boats Over Performance
item.description: The US Navy will no longer buy a highly prized — but ultimately troubled — drone speedboat manufactured by Aevex Corp.’s BlackSea after already spending more than $130 million on the technology, according to people briefed on the matter.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Manson
